title: Do not allow me to create a short cut to sent a text with Win Shift A

judgment.rationale: The report identifies the intended shortcut and text result, but it does not show the actual Keyboard Manager configuration or whether the shortcut is being captured as a text mapping versus being swallowed before injection.
evidence: The reporter expects Win+Shift+A to insert text like “Fish Space Toy@”.
The area is described as Keyboard Manager and the report references the manual, but no screenshot or exact configuration is attached.
There is no maintainer reply, bug report ZIP, or narrowed repro in a specific target app.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the saved shortcut-to-text configuration and a focused current repro before deciding whether this is a Keyboard Manager shortcut-capture bug or a configuration mismatch.

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue may still require a code change, but the current public thread does not yet show whether the intended mapping was saved and triggered in the supported path.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says they followed the Keyboard Manager manual to create a shortcut that should insert text when pressing Win+Shift+A, but nothing happens when the shortcut is used.
known_information: The report is on PowerToys 0.100.2 from a per-user Microsoft Store install on Windows 10 build 19045.
The expected behavior is text insertion, not a normal shortcut remap.
The issue body does not include a screenshot of the saved mapping, the target application, or whether the UI successfully captured Win+Shift+A during setup.
inferences: The missing distinction is whether the shortcut-to-text mapping was stored as intended or whether the Windows-key combination is being consumed before Keyboard Manager injects text.
Because Keyboard Manager does support text mappings, the issue is not obviously a feature request, but it is still under-specified.
issue_context.analysis: This is a classic case where the right next step is configuration evidence rather than more generic logs. A screenshot of the saved mapping and one controlled reproduction in a named app will tell triage whether the problem is in shortcut capture, persistence, or text injection.
initial_investigation: Keyboard Manager currently exposes text mappings and validates them through src/modules/KeyboardManager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs, so a shortcut-to-text workflow does exist.
The current issue text does not show the saved mapping or prove that Win+Shift+A was accepted and stored in the expected text-mapping path.

information_gaps.information: A screenshot of the exact shortcut-to-text mapping as saved in Keyboard Manager.
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms the real trigger keys, remap type, and target text instead of inferring them from the translated issue description.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Open Keyboard Manager, show the saved text-mapping row, and upload a screenshot through the GitHub web UI.

information_gaps.information: A numbered repro in one named target app, including whether the same text mapping works with a non-Windows-key shortcut such as Ctrl+Shift+A.
information_gaps.why_needed: That separates a general text-injection failure from a Windows-key shortcut-capture problem.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List the exact setup and test steps, then say whether a simpler non-Win shortcut works in the same target app.

information_gaps.information: Whether Keyboard Manager captures and displays Win+Shift+A exactly as expected while the mapping is being created.
information_gaps.why_needed: If the editor never stores the intended trigger correctly, triage should investigate capture/validation rather than runtime injection.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with whether the editor shows Win+Shift+A during setup and whether the final saved row still shows the same shortcut.

actions.label: Request shortcut-to-text configuration evidence

comment.body:
Thanks for describing the intended shortcut and text output. To narrow this to the correct Keyboard Manager path, please provide:

1. A screenshot of the exact shortcut-to-text mapping as it is saved in Keyboard Manager.
2. Short numbered steps in one named target app, including whether the same text mapping works if you use a non-Windows-key shortcut such as Ctrl+Shift+A.
3. Confirmation that Keyboard Manager captured and displayed Win+Shift+A correctly while you created the mapping.

That will tell us whether this is a shortcut-capture problem, a saved-configuration mismatch, or a runtime text-injection bug.
